polity.canonical_name_en: Buyid Realm of Fars and Iraq

activity.notes: From 977 Adud al-Dawla directly ruled both Fars and Iraq and became the most powerful Buyid monarch, remaining in control until his death in March 983. ATLAS separates this expanded phase from his earlier Fars-only rule.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica — Fārs iii. History in the Islamic Period
sources.citation_text: Iranica explicitly gives Adud al-Dawla's rule in Fars and Iraq from 977 to 983.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica — ʿAŻOD-AL-DAWLA, ABŪ ŠOJĀʾ FANNĀ ḴOSROW
sources.citation_text: Iranica describes Adud al-Dawla as the greatest Buyid monarch and notes that at his death in 983 he directly ruled Fars, Iraq, and adjacent territories.

review_context.correction_note: Add the historically distinct expanded Fars-Iraq phase.
